title: Reed Mere
shortDescription: Still water, cut reed, and a light with no lantern.
longDescription:
The mere is black tea and iron, smaller than the peat-cut and meaner about reflections. Cut reed lies in bundles. Reedcutter Sile watches the water as if it had taken a voice.
South is the mist-lane.

fixtures.name: Reedcutter Sile
fixtures.lookDescription: A toad in oiled wool, reed-knife on a cord, not raised. Try talk sile.
fixtures.examineDescription: A toad in oiled wool, with a reed-knife on a cord knotted short so the blade always hangs point-down. Eleven years of cutting has worn a groove across the palm of her right paw. She has been close enough to that light to hold a paw over it, and she says it did not warm her. She will not call it a ghost and does not like being asked to.
fixtures.dialogue: Sile has a bundle of cut reed under one arm and her knife corded down against her hip. "Hobb sent you, or you wandered out here. Comes to the same thing." She tips her chin at the water. "I have cut this mere eleven years. Last week I called to my brother across it and got nothing back, and he was standing in the reeds hearing me fine. Whatever is sitting on that water is keeping things. Talk sile and I will show you. Do not drink it."

fixtures.name: Still Water
fixtures.lookDescription: Water that does not give your face back. Examine it.
fixtures.examineDescription: The mere should show sky. It shows reed, and then it shows a light with no lantern under it. Your face is not in it. Sile says that is the problem, and she says it without poetry.
